intro: Your published section is on the left. My version is on the right, with new words highlighted and cut words struck. It's in the article so far as a candidate, not accepted until you say so.

Pangram's web app: the whole section reads 100% Human (1,004 words scanned, 18:02:27 UTC, batch 227g). The published section read 100% AI. Every paragraph passes alone, or beside a neighbor that passes alone when it's under 50 words.

The gate ran three rounds: meaning traces, cold reads, and the whole-article stance check. What they found in my wording is fixed, except three things I kept because every other wording failed Pangram. They're below, with how many wordings I tried and my opinion. My Human/AI calls for this section: 171 of 233 right (73%); saying AI every time would have been right 44%.

Kept 1, P8: "even just general reputation". The trace says "even just" ranks reputation as the weakest lever. Two wordings without it read AI. My opinion: it sounds like you, and the point (the levers all lead to one person) is the same.
Kept 2, P15: "a lot of power". The traces call "a lot of" added intensity (published: "power over people"). Five wordings without it each failed a check. My opinion: fine.

Kept 3, P15: "when things are required as pre-reqs … it can put … in the hands of the gatekeepers". Cold readers asked which things, what "it" is, and who the gatekeepers are. Five wordings that name the gatekeeper failed beside P14. The trace reads it as the published meaning. My opinion: "pre-reqs" makes it clear enough; if you want it airtight, write that sentence yourself, since your own sentences pass.

About the published text (the reviewers', for you to decide): "willing to be seen" isn't introduced anywhere in the article; "Founderism" is never defined; P4's questions come right before "the four questions" (I added "about the founder" to P6); reviewers, circles and ZEGG Forum aren't explained here (ZEGG Forum is linked). Three contradictions: the boundary in P16 against the medicine prerequisite, which is a gate on other people; two thresholds (several signs together deserve attention, but diagnosing dissent means leave now); and, new today, your own land ("if people end up living on land I buy") against "no individual controls admission" when whoever owns the land holds the power.
Changes under your word rules: "boring power" is "practical power" (your 12:22 message), and P19's "one of the most efficient sentences ever invented" quip is "pretty much a conversation ender".
